thread:
sam_sre: Heads up — since the RBAC push at 11:10 UTC we're seeing a spike in mTLS handshake failures for service-to-service calls in ap-south and eu-west. Errors look like KMS unwrap denies when the cert rotator tries to fetch ephemeral private keys.

mike_security: can you paste a sample error?

sam_sre: sure — log from proxy (truncated):

```
2026-03-23T11:12:33Z proxy[ingress] WARN handshake failed: tls: failed to configure private key: kms:DecryptAccessDenied: access denied for key projects/prod/keys/ephemeral-rotator
caused_by: IAMPolicyBindingDenial: principal serviceAccount:rotator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com missing roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

priya_platform: that role change was part of the RBAC sweep. We tightened serviceAccount scopes for a handful of infra roles — rotator might have been in-scope.

jen_oncall: observed user impact: spike in 5xx for async inference routing, some canary traffic fell back to warmer models. Incident metrics: TLS handshake failure rate + service-to-service error rate correlated with rotator job schedule.

sam_sre: mitigation idea: rollback the RBAC commit for the rotator service account and temporarily allow decrypt, or configure the rotator to use a fallback key in a different KMS project. Which is faster?

mike_security: rollback is fastest. We need an audit trail before changing roles: grab the IAM change diff and KMS audit logs (accessTransparency and CloudAudit). Also check whether the rotator used a delegated principal or an intermediate token that we revoked.

priya_platform: I can revert the PR if we confirm the serviceAccount id. PR number is 3421. If we roll back, note: the previous role had broader scope — we'll schedule a follow-up to scope it properly.

sam_sre: also seeing a smaller set of errors with session ticket resumption failing post-handshake — likely because the ephemeral key never registered so session resumption keys missing. Example snippet: `tls: client session ticket decrypt failed: key not found`

mike_security: include KMS logs query:`resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt" AND jsonPayload.status.code=7`

jen_oncall: I ran a query and found ~120 Deny events between 11:09–11:18 UTC from rotator SA in ap-south1. Also 3 from a staging rotator in eu-west1.

priya_platform: I'm going to open a short rollback and leave a tiny emergency exception for the rotator SA while we craft a least-privileged policy. Will annotate in the PR.

sam_sre: for the outage postmortem, can we capture: exact IAM binding change, KMS key ACLs, which rotator pod versions attempted unwrap, and whether any key versions were rotated at the same time?

mike_security: yes. Add audit log exports for that day to the incident folder. Also verify there are no lateral privilege escalations from the rollback window.

priya_platform: rolling back now — revert PR 3421, creating emergency exception entry: `iam:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` -> serviceAccount:rotator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Will add TTL 1h.

deploy-bot: revert PR 3421 merged by priya_platform at 2026-03-23T11:20:05Z :white_check_mark:

sam_sre: confirmed handshake failure rate starting to fall within 2 minutes of revert. Can we also add a circuit-breaker fallback in proxy to avoid cascading failures when rotator is unavailable?

mike_security: good call — add a short-term policy in proxy: if rotator unwrap fails, allow proxy to use cached key for 10s instead of failing closed. We'll need config change and a short changelog entry for security review.

priya_platform: creating a post-incident task: 1) repro in staging with RBAC tighten, 2) create least-privileged KMS role for rotator using IAM Condition (restrict by serviceAccount and key name), 3) add circuit-breaker and observability for unwrap latency, 4) update runbook to include immediate KMS unwrap checks.

jen_oncall: adding alerts: KMS DecryptAccessDenied > 5 in 5m for any production key -> pager. Also handshake-failure rate > 1% for 5m -> page oncall.

sam_sre: one more ask — check inter-region fallback behavior. We saw eu-west canary traffic hit ap-south rotator endpoints (cross-region). Make sure role bindings are consistent across projects/regions so rotator won't be allowed in one region and denied in another during rollouts.

mike_security: will diff IAM bindings across projects and ensure a rotation plan that updates bindings before removing privileges.

priya_platform: closing the emergency window in 1h after we confirm no residual denys. Will follow up with a write-up in #postmortems and link to the audit export.

sam_sre: thanks — please paste the audit export link once available and tag me. :thumbsup:

mike_security: noted. collecting logs now and will attach to the incident page.
